post.caption: He hid his machine in the Alps. Daniel Swarovski came from a family of glass cutters in Bohemia. After a Vienna electrical exhibition in 1883, he built a machine that cut crystal faster and more precisely than hands could, and he filed a patent in 1892. In 1895, he started a company with two partners and put the factory in Wattens, in the Austrian Alps, for water power. The remote spot also helped protect his secrets. His first logo, from 1899, was the edelweiss, an Alpine flower. The Crystal Worlds museum opened in Wattens in 1995, and the company's 2018 star on the Rockefeller Center tree held 3 million crystals.
